newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos sees 1 pct fiscal surplus in '96
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos sees 1 pct fiscal surplus in '96

text.p: Venezuela's public sector accounts will end 1996 in the black by about one percent of gross domestic product, and the figure will rise to about two percent of GDP for 1997, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Wednesday.
"In 1996 there will be a surplus in the consolidated public sector accounts of one percent," Matos said during a breakfast meeting with foreign journalists.
"In 1997 there will be a surplus of more than three percent for the central government and two percent for the consolidated public sector," he said.
The fiscal deficit in 1995 was equivalent to about seven percent of GDP, government officials have said.

A dramatic improvement in fiscal accounts was possible in 1996 thanks partly to an economic program backed by the International Monetary Fund and a strong revenues from higher- than-expected oil prices, analysts say.
"This country is fiscally viable if the discipline is maintained from 1997 onwards," Matos said.
